**ACCEPT** — `domain:devx @ objectui` execution seat, PM session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, R46, reviewed 2026-09-07T17:00Z against GitHub and the tree, ⛔ never against the report's narrative.

## The fences held, checked mechanically rather than read

The diff is 2 files, `+306/-16`, draft, head `679242dba`, based on `47053c9f6` — the post-#8391 tip, so this builds on the resolver rather than racing it. Scanning the gate's patch for every fenced identifier returns **zero touched lines** for `isCovered`, `coveredPrefixes`, `COVERED_SPECIFIERS` and `and their subpaths judged`. #8117 is not folded in.

## The repair is the right shape, and the reason is in what it refuses without being told to

`operandDenotes()` replaces a *mention* test with a small whole-expression grammar whose stated invariant is that the operand's **key set is the real module's, so it grows when the real module grows**. That is the property the gate actually needs, and the evidence it is the property rather than a list of known evasions is that the **array** form is refused without ever having been designed for — one rule closing a class, not two instances. ⭐ The object-literal exclusion is taken deliberately even where the contents would inherit (`...{ ...actual }`), argued in the header, and pinned; the one nesting that would be correct spells the same thing as `...actual` and no site writes it.

## The load-bearing measurement is the one this dispatch demanded, and it is honest about its own scope

**625 judged / 625 inherit / 0 frozen before and after, with all 625 rows diffed PER SITE on verdict *and* reason string against the base gate — byte-identical.** That is the "prove no false refusal by census, ⛔ not by inspection" requirement met exactly. The nine distinct operand shapes the tree actually writes are enumerated and each pinned as its own case, so the accept side is defended by construction and not by the aggregate count.

⭐ **And the dev caught two of its own implementation bugs with that census before delivering** — the first `operandDenotes` omitted `<`/`>` from the bracket-pairing table, so generic argument lists would not strip and the census fell from 625 inherit to **41**: 584 false refusals. That is precisely the failure this brief was most worried about, it was found by the instrument rather than by eye, and it is reported rather than quietly fixed. This is why the census requirement was not ceremony.

## ⭐ The report's most valuable line is the one that limits its own claim

> The GATE itself still exits 0 under the ablation. No call site in this tree writes the C or D shape, so the repo scan cannot see this defect at all — the pins are the only thing that can.

⇒ The acceptance criterion "reverting your change turns your new pins red" is satisfied by the **pins**, ⛔ not by the gate's exit code, and the dev says so instead of letting the green stand in for proof. Same shape as #8383's non-vacuity leg this afternoon: an assertion is only worth what its ability to say *no* is worth. The ablation proves the mutation landed on disk (blob `0b79902ca` → `a83202dbe`, removed-text count 0, injected-text count 1) **before** any result was read, and the harness exits 90/91/92 rather than reporting a pass if any of those preconditions fail.

⚠️ The dev also declines to count a sixth refusal that was already frozen on the base (`...(importOriginal)` — the old mention test also required a `(` after the token). Reported as a regression guard rather than as new-behaviour evidence. ⛔ Not padding the result is worth as much as the result.

## ⚠️ One observation from this review, filed as a note rather than a change request

`closingIndex` / `openingIndex` treat `<` and `>` as an unconditional bracket pair. TypeScript's grammar is genuinely ambiguous there — a `=>` or a comparison inside an operand would skew the depth counter, and `beforeTypeAssertion` walks that same counter. **On today's measured population this is zero-risk**: none of the nine operand shapes in the tree contains either, and the per-site diff is empty. It is recorded because the failure direction matters — it would surface as a **false refusal**, which reds CI loudly on correct code rather than passing silently, so it is self-announcing rather than latent. ⛔ No change requested and no card filed: a hypothetical with no occurrence is not a finding.

## Two corrections to this seat's own dispatch, both the dev's and both right

1. The brief said C and D belong in the pin's **negative-control** block. By that file's own vocabulary a negative control is *correct code that must never be flagged*, and a positive control is a *failure shape* — so C and D went into the positive-control block and the four new accept-side counterexamples into the negative-control block. The dev used the file's definitions over the brief's wording and said so.
2. The brief referred to "the member-access forms the file already documents". Measured: the header documents no member-access form at all (its only documented non-trivial shape is the `(orig as any)()` cast-then-call), and no site in the tree uses one. The dev accepted member access because the brief explicitly required it, then **wrote the missing justification into the header** — a property read keeps a key set the module owns — and pinned it. Documenting rather than transcribing was the right call.

No changeset owed (`scripts/**` only; `check-changeset-presence` agrees). Not governed surface (`--test` on both paths ⇒ NOT GOVERNED). One NOT-MEASURED result is recorded rather than reported as a pass: a first byte-hygiene call hit `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on a wrong script name before the correct `check:control-bytes` was run green.

Next: CI convergence → flip ready → post-flip guard → auto-merge SQUASH → queue confirmation → landing probe (`operandDenotes` present on re-fetched `origin/main` with `<`/`>` in both bracket-pair tables; control: the census still reads **625 judged / 625 inherit / 0 frozen**, i.e. the ratchet did not move and nothing was newly refused) → LANDED here and on #8183, which closes via `Fixes`.

⇒ **#6892 becomes dispatchable once this lands** — it is the last card queued on this file.

**Content probe on re-fetched `origin/main` (tip `fff250ff1`, read 2026-09-07T17:30Z)** — the Armed note's two claims:

1. **`operandDenotes` present** at `scripts/check-vi-mock-inherit.mjs:1180`, and `holdsObtainedModule()` is retained as the named entry point now delegating to it (`:1235-1238`) — `return operandDenotes(text, token, tokenIsValue) === 'module';` — so both call sites (`:1408` binding propagation, `:1434` the spread decision) go through the new grammar with no third path left behind.
2. **The bug that produced 584 false refusals is fixed on the merged tree**, which is why this and not the headline was chosen as the probe: `<`/`>` appear in **both** bracket-pair tables — `closingIndex` at `:1098` and `openingIndex` at `:1111`.

**Control — taken from the gate RUNNING on merged `main`, not from a source grep.** The post-merge push run of `Inert vi.mock Specifiers` ([34147701330](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/34147701330), head `fff250ff1`, step completed 17:27:57Z) prints:

```
✅  check-vi-mock-inherit: OK (4458 tracked source file(s), 2724 test-named; 616 carry a mock;
    625 call site(s) on … and their subpaths judged (625 inherit, 0 auto-mocked);
    35 other workspace, 243 external, 879 local, 0 non-static, …)
```

⇒ **625 judged / 625 inherit / 0 frozen on main after the change** — byte-for-byte the census the dev measured before it. **Zero false refusals landed.** ⭐ That is the reading that matters here: the whole risk of this PR was tightening a recogniser too far, the dev's own first attempt did exactly that (625 → 41 inherit), and the merged tree is measured — by the gate itself, in CI, on `main` — to have moved nothing. A source grep could not have told us that.

Incidentally the same line re-confirms #8391 an hour on: the verdict reads `… and their subpaths judged`, with `35 other workspace`.
